quest.title: The Tale-Telling Heart
quest.description: A group of people, each with their own story to tell, lights a bonfire at Blue Amber Lake...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x400, Primogem x50, Mora x30000, Hero's Wit x5, Mystic Enhancement Ore x4

chapter.title: East of the Moon, West of the Sun

dialogues.speaker: Danyusha Shesternin
dialogues.text: Yes. Since the Proof of the Cognoscenti is well within reach, we might have a chance at getting it too.

dialogues.speaker: Danyusha Shesternin
dialogues.text: It may not be as valuable as the Great Treasure, but it's an essential key for those who covet said treasure...

dialogues.speaker: Zhorik Shesternin
dialogues.text: ...Yes. You're right.

dialogues.speaker: Danyusha Shesternin
dialogues.text: I think we could perhaps use it to buy ourselves some time to turn things around... Zhorik, are you listening?

dialogues.speaker: Zhorik Shesternin
dialogues.text: I'm listening. You're right, you're right. However...

dialogues.speaker: Danyusha Shesternin
dialogues.text: So it's a tragedy, isn't it? He gave up the reward, and when he returned home, nothing was the same...

dialogues.speaker: Zhorik Shesternin
dialogues.text: Why tell the story of a fool like him? If it were me, I'd have stayed on that island. Apples aren't my favorite, but that'd hardly be an issue.

dialogues.speaker: Tolfin
dialogues.text: Looks like we have new friends joining us.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehe, this is a nice place to rest. Are you all telling stories?

dialogues.speaker: Zhorik Shesternin
dialogues.text: Tch, more people...

dialogues.speaker: Danyusha Shesternin
dialogues.text: Zhorik, be nice. Sorry, he's probably feeling unwell. Been like this since we left Novokitezhgrad...

dialogues.speaker: Tolfin
dialogues.text: Let us introduce ourselves first. I'm Tolfin. As you can see, I deal in little odds and ends and tell a few stories.

dialogues.speaker: Tolfin
dialogues.text: These two are Mr. and Mrs. Shesternin, who are on their way back to Novokitezhgrad from Nasha Town, I believe. This trail is a tough one. Brave of you two to make the attempt.

dialogues.speaker: Danyusha Shesternin
dialogues.text: Ah... We have our reasons for coming here, but that's personal and a long story, so let's leave it at that.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #It's our turn now, right? Paimon's Paimon, and {M#he}{F#she} is {NICKNAME}. We're adventurers, just passing by.

dialogues.speaker: Tolfin
dialogues.text: Oh? Then you must have heard of Reed Miller's Great Treasure. They say that the key to unlocking its secret lies within the five <color=#00E1FFFF>Proofs of the Cognoscenti</color>.

choices.text: Treasure hunting is in the blood of an adventurer.

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: Speaking of that, I've told many stories about Reed Miller, and I was fortunate enough to lay my eyes on a Proof of the Cognoscenti. One of them was even found by my friend.

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: Coincidentally, this very spot we're resting at was built by that friend of mine. Knowing him, the Proof of the Cognoscenti might very well be here.

response.speaker: Zhorik Shesternin
response.text: ...Are you talking about Papa Wrench?

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: Oh-ho, it appears my friend is quite famous. Back then, he was traveling between the islands with a caravan, and as it happened, I would have some dealings with them.

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: Come to think of it, his story is quite extraordinary. Although he lost his memory due to an accident, his skill in crafting and maintaining machinery is as remarkable as ever.

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: And the very accident that caused his memory loss, that shipwreck from many years ago... I'm sure you've heard of it too, Mr. and Mrs. Shesternin. I believe him to be a survivor of that incident.

response.speaker: Danyusha Shesternin
response.text: That's... Could there be such a coincidence...? Zhorik survived that incident, too... but my father wasn't as lucky.

response.speaker: Zhorik Shesternin
response.text: Danyusha, didn't we agree to leave all that behind?

response.speaker: Danyusha Shesternin
response.text: Yes, I know... but lately I've been thinking... Father loved me — loved us — so much. Were he still alive, he wouldn't sit and let this happen...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Are you two in trouble? Perhaps we could help.

response.speaker: Zhorik Shesternin
response.text: You? Right, you're adventurers... Then, could you find the Great Treasure for us?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: As long as the treasure exists, we will find it! But, we can't just let you take the Great Treasure off our hands for free either.

response.speaker: Zhorik Shesternin
response.text: Heh, money, money, money... It all comes down to money in the end. Nothing's negotiable without Mora, is that it?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Why are you suddenly so agitated...? You're the one commissioning us to find something for you, so of course you need to compensate us.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We enjoy helping others, sure, but it's not right to expect us to work for free!

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: Working for free... The Papa Wrench I knew was exactly that sort of person.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Eh? But how would he make a living like that?

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: He was lucky that the caravan leader looked after him. If it weren't for that, I don't think he would have lasted so long.

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: He only charged nominal fees for making and repairing machinery. Sometimes he even did it for free. He did the same when it came to teaching others about machines, sharing his knowledge without reserve.

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: The children in the caravan loved him too, because he had endless stories to tell... Though I should clarify, I could go toe to toe with him on that.

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: Too bad I didn't prepare candies for my audience like he did, though. His little listeners were, without exception, all captivated by the sweet candies and fantastical stories.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Now you've gotten Paimon all curious about meeting him! It must've been fun listening to his stories... Oh, Paimon wants to hear about how he found the Proof of the Cognoscenti!

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: Unfortunately, he's no longer with us.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? But you were saying...

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: He built all the mechanical devices here for a child called Tinet. She was rendered eccentric and hard to get along with by an illness that tormented her.

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: It took Papa Wrench quite some time to get close to her, too. These devices were originally made to make her happy and fulfill a small wish of hers...

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: But that poor child didn't make it. After that, Papa Wrench also passed away from his chronic illness and overwhelming grief.

response.speaker: Danyusha Shesternin
response.text: *sigh*... How do you have so many sad stories to tell?

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: Madam, you're mistaken. Other than tragedies, I also have plenty of stories about righteous bandits robbing the rich to help the poor and tales of underdogs getting their revenge to share. But for now...

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: Perhaps the two of you could provide some story material. How about a family-friendly treasure-hunting tale? The treasure in this case would, of course, be the Proof of the Cognoscenti that Papa Wrench left behind.

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: He once said that, should he pass, all his belongings would be mine to handle as I see fit. I'm sure he wouldn't mind a couple of adventurers taking it in exchange for a great story.

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: "After a thrilling adventure by the mirror-sheened Blue Amber Lake, the two adventurers find the treasure at last." Cliche, perhaps, but a captivating evergreen tale nonetheless.

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: What do you think?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: In that case, we'd be happy to. But umm, rather than our story, could you tell us more about Papa Wrench later?

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: Haha, no problem. Like I said, all the mechanical devices here were built to make Tinet happy. According to Papa Wrench's vision...

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: Tinet would need go on a quest like a true adventurer — <color=#00E1FFFF>she'd have to collect lots of Stellafruit, deliver them to Sergeant Octopus, and pass the trial to awaken Colonel Iron Whale</color>.

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: Then, the "Proof of the Cognoscenti" would be her reward. Hmm, that's all the hints I can give for now. If you two run into any difficulty, just think of this as extra spice in our story.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It's alright, Papa Wrench wouldn't make anything too tough on purpose, right? This should be way easier than those mechanisms in the ruins.

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: Alright, then! Show me what you're capable of. Sergeant Octopus has command over two areas, and you can start the challenge from either one.

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: As for you, Mr. and Mrs. Shesternin, since you're just passing through and don't intend to be held up by this treasure hunt, please excuse me if I accompany you no further.

response.speaker: Zhorik Shesternin
response.text: ...Of course, but we'll stay here for a little while longer.

choices.text: Sure, with fair compensation for honest work...
For Paimon's sake, I must obtain the Great Treasure...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Y—You're doing this for Paimon? Paimon's touched... When we get the Great Treasure, she'll share half of it with you for sure, {NICKNAME}!

talks.objective: Collect Stellafruit, deliver them to Sergeant Octopus, and pass the trial

dialogues.speaker: Zhorik Shesternin
dialogues.text: It must be here...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What are you doing here?

dialogues.speaker: Zhorik Shesternin
dialogues.text: Not much. I just wanted to watch your treasure hunt from the place with the best view.

talks.objective: Collect Stellafruit, deliver them to Sergeant Octopus, and pass the trial

dialogues.speaker: Tolfin
dialogues.text: Stellafruit only grow near Blue Amber Lake, and the climate here is indeed very different from everywhere else. The atmosphere in the air... is beyond words.

dialogues.speaker: Tolfin
dialogues.text: You need to deliver enough Stellafruit before Sergeant Octopus will reveal the trial's contents. Well, since this is a fairy tale, I suppose it doesn't really count as "bribery."

dialogues.speaker: Tolfin
dialogues.text: I guess I'll come visit Colonel Iron Whale from time to time.

choices.text: About the Proofs of the Cognoscenti...

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: They make for great stories, so I do know a thing or two. Allegedly, there are five Proofs of the Cognoscenti in total.

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: Besides the one Papa Wrench had, there are two more on the three southern islands. The remaining two are further north. You might find more clues about them in Piramida.

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: If you're also interested in the Great Treasure, you might want to keep an eye out for them.

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: A journey needs empathetic companions, no? It had quite the natural gift, so training it didn't take long at all.

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: Maybe it's because I have a special connection with weasel thieves — which I suppose you could call a family tradition too, hmm?

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: I wish you a lovely journey.

dialogues.speaker: Danyusha Shesternin
dialogues.text: Will I make it in time...?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Are you leaving?

dialogues.speaker: Danyusha Shesternin
dialogues.text: ...Oh! Yes, yes. I left something important in Nasha Town, so I should go back...

dialogues.speaker: Tolfin
dialogues.text: It seems the device for awakening Colonel Iron Whale is missing some parts. That figures. Even guarded treasures are coveted by others, let alone unguarded ones.

dialogues.speaker: Zhorik Shesternin
dialogues.text: So the Proof of the Cognoscenti... the treasure is hidden here?

dialogues.speaker: Tolfin
dialogues.text: It's certainly nearby, but...

dialogues.speaker: Zhorik Shesternin
dialogues.text: Why don't we just take it apart, then? It's little more than a pile of scrap anyway. This way, you won't have to play this little game of pretend anymore. Why not just make things easier?

choices.text: That's certainly one way to go about it...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey! That's... Um, Paimon doesn't think that's right. Papa Wrench poured his heart into this after all. If we can just find the missing parts...

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: If we're talking about spare parts, I might have some leads.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wow, are you really giving us clues just like that?

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: It's not unusual to receive aid from mysterious characters in stories, right? Mr. Shesternin, if you're also interested in the treasure's whereabouts, it's not too late to join us...

response.speaker: Zhorik Shesternin
response.text: Hah! I... I'm a collector, so of course I'm interested in the Proof of the Cognoscenti, but I won't play along with your childish games.

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: Well, you can certainly try to challenge Colonel Iron Whale your way. Let's see who can locate the treasure first. As for you, adventurers, please follow me.

choices.text: Time to spice up this story.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon's going to sneeze from all that spice! Hmm... there must be some other way! We just need to find the missing parts, right? Well, we're good at finding things.

dialogues.speaker: Tolfin
dialogues.text: Papa Wrench's workshop is down this way. You should be able to find the spare parts there.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Then all we need to do is activate the lift, right? Paimon's got this... Huh? Where's the lever?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah! A weasel thief!? Did it steal the lever?

dialogues.speaker: Tolfin
dialogues.text: Well, this is... unexpected. Don't worry, I'll handle things from here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You? But...

dialogues.speaker: Tolfin
dialogues.text: Huginn! It's your turn to shine.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eh!? And where did you come from!?

dialogues.speaker: Tolfin
dialogues.text: It's not that unusual for traveling merchants to have a few clever companions, no? Quickly, let's catch up to it.

dialogues.speaker: Zhorik Shesternin
dialogues.text: Just a hunk of metal junk...

dialogues.speaker: Zhorik Shesternin
dialogues.text: Haha, you're too late. You didn't find the Proof of the Cognoscenti up there, did you?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? How did you...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Sure, but we found something more precious still!

dialogues.speaker: Zhorik Shesternin
dialogues.text: More precious? Impossible...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Judging by that smug look he's wearing, he probably found the Proof ahead of us. Might as well try to trick him here...)

dialogues.speaker: Tolfin
dialogues.text: (Oh? You want me to play along with your little act, then?)

dialogues.speaker: Tolfin
dialogues.text: Well... there are five Proofs of the Cognoscenti after all, nor would locating the Great Treasure be a simple affair even after one collects them all.

dialogues.speaker: Tolfin
dialogues.text: So... I would hardly be surprised if something in Papa Wrench's collection could far surpass a single Proof in value.

dialogues.speaker: Zhorik Shesternin
dialogues.text: ...Such an item exists?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: O—Of course! You could call it priceless, even!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #(Paimon has no idea what {NICKNAME}'s up to, but... That isn't exactly a lie, right? Memories are priceless! Besides...)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...J—Just ask Tolfin or something. He'd pick what we've got over the Proof for sure!

dialogues.speaker: Zhorik Shesternin
dialogues.text: And what would a wandering merchant like him know? ... Aha! I get it now, brat. You're bitter because you lost, aren't you? You're upset that I didn't need to play your little game to get the treasure.

dialogues.speaker: Zhorik Shesternin
dialogues.text: I happen to be in a good mood, so I'll pass this advice to you for free: Forget about the rules. People who stick to them hardly ever get the life they desire.

dialogues.speaker: Zhorik Shesternin
dialogues.text: Fortune favors those who think outside the box, like me. See? You did all that work, in the end, you still couldn't find the Proof of the Cognoscenti.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Zhorik takes out a pristine and opulent goblet. It is hard to believe that it also belonged to Papa Wrench's collection...

dialogues.speaker: Tolfin
dialogues.text: Now, now. It is indeed true that one of the five Proofs of the Cognoscenti is a goblet. But as far as I know, that one is in the Fatui's possession — or was, before someone stole it from them.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Ooh, and would you look at that? It's right here in my backpack.

dialogues.speaker: Tolfin
dialogues.text: Haha, it seems your fate and Reed Miller's were destined to intersect.

dialogues.speaker: Tolfin
dialogues.text: The Proof that Papa Wrench found was a mask, and he would often let the children play with it.

dialogues.speaker: Tolfin
dialogues.text: As for this goblet... I do believe it's a gift the caravan leader brought from Snezhnograd. Ah, but Papa Wrench never could bring himself to use such a precious thing.

dialogues.speaker: Tolfin
dialogues.text: #It's valuable, of course, but nothing compared to the Proof of the Cognoscenti... Which in turn makes it even less valuable than the treasure {NICKNAME} found, I fear.

dialogues.speaker: Zhorik Shesternin
dialogues.text: That's impossible...

dialogues.speaker: Tolfin
dialogues.text: It appears even a seasoned collector such as you can be mistaken at times, Mr. Shesternin. If it sets your mind at ease, you are free to find an appraiser for it when you return to Novokitezhgrad.

dialogues.speaker: Zhorik Shesternin
dialogues.text: ...Where is the real Proof of the Cognoscenti then? No... forget that. What's the treasure you spoke of, kid? The one you claim is the superior find...

dialogues.speaker: Zhorik Shesternin
dialogues.text: You may have beaten me, but I shan't accept it until you've shown me what you found.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Th—That's...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: (The picture and memories might be priceless to Tolfin, but could we really say something like "This is the most valuable treasure!" without embarrassing ourselves!?)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #(Hurry, {NICKNAME}! Think of something!)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Since there's more to what happened aboard the "Fortunate One" ten years ago...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Before we show you, take a look at this.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You show the picture from earlier to Zhorik...

dialogues.speaker: Zhorik Shesternin
dialogues.text: ...What is this trickery!? Who commissioned you to do this? Was it that old man? Is he still alive? Where is he!?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So you *are* the Zhorik that Papa Wrench mentioned!

dialogues.speaker: Zhorik Shesternin
dialogues.text: "Papa Wrench"... So, he lured me here with a fake name so he can have his revenge, is that it? You think you can take me?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Revenge? What are you talking about?... Wait, so the one who pushed Papa Wrench off the ship was...

dialogues.speaker: Zhorik Shesternin
dialogues.text: Drop the act. You're all working for that old man, aren't you? Wait... Does Danyusha know? Is she in on this too?

dialogues.speaker: Zhorik Shesternin
dialogues.text: That woman... She agreed so quickly because she knew this was a trap all along, didn't she? Offering to deliver the letter, doing all that, just to isolate me...?

response.speaker: Zhorik Shesternin
response.text: No. Not one of you will ever get me! Not you, and not that old man!

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Zhorik scurries away, not even bothering with the precious goblet he mistook for the Proof of the Cognoscenti...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Are you just letting him go? We don't have any grudge against him, but isn't Papa Wrench your friend?

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: Don't worry. The path he took looks most dangerous. I would not be surprised if something happens to him.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What do you mean...?

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: I mean that Papa Wrench has many other friends aside from me. Besides, who doesn't love a story where justice is served?

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: I'm afraid ten years wasn't long enough to change his ways. If he had proven himself a changed man, even just a little, then I would have forgiven him, per Papa Wrench's wishes.

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: Alas, like many others, he too is a prisoner to his baser instincts. What a tragedy.

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: ...What saddens me more is the lack of a winner in our little treasure-hunting game. *sigh* No new story material for me, then.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh! Paimon almost forgot — where exactly is the Proof of the Cognoscenti? Will we find it here? Um... can we ask Huginn for help?

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: Might this be what you're looking for?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: A mask... Is this it!? But how... You had it on you this whole time?

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: Haha, not quite. Zhorik did find it first, but he thought the flashier, fancier goblet was the real Proof, so he tossed the mask aside.

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: And now that he's forfeited it, the treasure is yours.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Feels like a freebie... but wait! We worked hard for it too! It's our just reward!

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: That's right. If you end up revealing the Great Treasure's secrets... Well, that would make for a fascinating story.

talks.objective: Follow Huginn and look for clues

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: (test)Readable Placeholder

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This isn't a spare part... Did Papa Wrench leave this here? So it's like Tolfin said. He stayed for Tinet's sake...

dialogues.speaker: Tolfin
dialogues.text: I didn't expect Huginn to dig up something like this. But judging by your words... Did you doubt what I said?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Well, they did come from someone who'd give away a friend's treasure...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #...Huh. When you put it like that, {NICKNAME}, it does sound suspicious! P—Paimon was just playing along earlier, just so you know! We had to see what tricks you had up your sleeve!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #What are you planning now, bringing us to this place?... Best be warned, {NICKNAME}'s super strong!

dialogues.speaker: Tolfin
dialogues.text: Haha. To me, you are both unexpected guests, but great "spices" for the story all the same. I can hardly thank you enough. Why would I ever mean you harm?

dialogues.speaker: Tolfin
dialogues.text: Well then, let's keep searching for the spare parts. I really don't know where Papa Wrench left the Proof of the Cognoscenti, so it's all on you now.

talks.objective: Follow Huginn and look for clues
Follow Huginn and look for clues

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? What's going on here?

dialogues.speaker: Tolfin
dialogues.text: Hmm, it seems Sergeant Octopus isn't feeling well. Perhaps it's getting aggressive because it's not used to the environment. After all, underground caves aren't exactly where octopuses usually hang out.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Your power is essential in awakening Colonel Iron Whale, Sergeant!... Um, so how exactly do we make it stop?

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: #Looks like we'll have to get closer to make it stop. Well then, I'll leave it to you, {NICKNAME} and Paimon.

choices.text: I feel like you're implying something here...

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: I've always respected the audience's freedom of interpretation. However, rather than that which lies between the lines, we have more pressing matters to address right now.

dialogues.speaker: Tolfin
dialogues.text: Should I recite a few silly limericks to set the mood? Hmm, perhaps not.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Phew, it finally stopped. Maybe this guy needs a demotion to "Corporal Octopus"!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #It's safe now, {NICKNAME}. Let's look around for the spare parts.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Three humans and a weasel search up and down, until you finally find the spare parts...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Awesome! Now we can go and wake Colonel Iron Whale up, right?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wh—What's going on? Ah! The path we came from has been blocked!

dialogues.speaker: Tolfin
dialogues.text: Oh? It looks like this is becoming quite the spicy story.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whether it's food or adventure, too much spice is bad news!

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: Don't worry, leave it to Huginn. Treasure-hunting isn't all it can do — it's also good at pathfinding.

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: You see? Just follow its lead, and we're bound to find something good.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, you... You're not gonna do anything yourself, are you? It's been on us or your Weasel Thief this whole time.

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: Haha, I suppose it's a kind of family tradition. Those who are bolder oft shall lead the charge, while all we can do is chronicle their feats and sing their praises.

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: Alright, our adventure isn't over yet. The Proof of the Cognoscenti awaits, so let's head out now.

talks.objective: Follow Huginn and find a way to return to the surface

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: (test)Readable Placeholder

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Same handwriting as earlier... Wait, Danyusha... Zhorik?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is Danyusha Papa Wrench's daughter, then? But Paimon thought he fell into the sea because of an accident that happened ten years ago aboard the Fortunate One.

dialogues.speaker: Tolfin
dialogues.text: *sigh* Huginn, you just had to dig this page out, didn't you? I guess I have no choice but to...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Paimon knew you were up to no good! {NICKNAME}, draw your sword, quick!

dialogues.speaker: Tolfin
dialogues.text: ...No choice but to tell you all my plans now, and ask that you pretend you know nothing from this point on.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Huh?

dialogues.speaker: Tolfin
dialogues.text: I was there the day Papa Wrench saw the obituary. He had a strange look on his face, so I asked him about the matter. Even so, he kept insisting that he couldn't remember the details from ten years ago.

dialogues.speaker: Tolfin
dialogues.text: Always assuming the best of others... That's just the way he was. Besides, he had Tinet to care for, so everything else took a backseat.

dialogues.speaker: Tolfin
dialogues.text: After he passed, I kept my ear to the ground, and what do you know? News reached me that the Shesternins had exhausted their wealth over the last ten years and had landed in serious debt.

dialogues.speaker: Tolfin
dialogues.text: So, I sent a messenger to tell a story. "Have you heard? The Proof of the Cognoscenti that can lead you to the Great Treasure is at the Blue Amber Lake in Nod-Krai"...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You were going to give him the Proof of the Cognoscenti?

dialogues.speaker: Tolfin
dialogues.text: Technically, it is Papa Wrench... Mr. Shesternin Sr.'s inheritance. As his legal heir, Zhorik has the right to it.

dialogues.speaker: Tolfin
dialogues.text: I'm not as charitable as ol' Papa, but I wanted to give Zhorik a chance to prove himself. And that's how the treasure hunt came to be.

dialogues.speaker: Tolfin
dialogues.text: He's not interested in the story or the setting, but he seems determined to get the Proof all the same. It's entirely possible that he might find it before you two.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That won't do!

dialogues.speaker: Tolfin
dialogues.text: Indeed. Therefore, my plan is to ask you to interfere with the process... or should I say, "finders keepers" — as long as you get it before him, of course.

dialogues.speaker: Tolfin
dialogues.text: Though if your conscience permits, you can let him find it first before taking it off his hands. Not a terrible strategy either, that.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So that's your plan... Paimon doesn't get it! Do you want him to have it or not? And, what if we didn't come this way? What was your original plan?

dialogues.speaker: Tolfin
dialogues.text: A scheme abandoned hardly matters in the present, does it? I have great faith in your treasure-hunting skills.

dialogues.speaker: Tolfin
dialogues.text: When we go back out, please pretend you've heard nothing. It would not do for me to appear biased, after all.

talks.objective: Follow Huginn and find a way to return to the surface
Follow Huginn and find a way to return to the surface

dialogues.speaker: Zhorik Shesternin
dialogues.text: So, you found the spare parts?

choices.text: Seems you're helpless against this hunk of metal junk.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe, we won! The Proof of the Cognoscenti is ours now!

response.speaker: Zhorik Shesternin
response.text: W—Well... congratulations. But are you really going to activate the device right now? This thing looks like it's been out of use for a while, there might be some malfunction...

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: Mr. Shesternin, are you worried that such a malfunction might hurt one of us? How thoughtful. However, with the treasure within our reach, it would be too much to ask us to simply ignore it.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Yeah, that's right! {NICKNAME}, let's install the parts and start it up right now!

choices.text: Guess it's up to us to awaken Colonel Iron Whale, then!

dialogues.speaker: Tolfin
dialogues.text: It's a shame that Tinet couldn't see all this with her own eyes. She would have loved it.

dialogues.speaker: Tolfin
dialogues.text: This must've been the gift that Papa Wrench wanted to give to Tinet... Shocking.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Did something shiny just fly upward...? W—Was that the Proof of the Cognoscenti!?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'll go up and take a look.

dialogues.speaker: Zhorik Shesternin
dialogues.text: You can climb up that thing?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Can we even call ourselves adventurers if we can't even manage that? Hmm, even if {NICKNAME} can't do it, Paimon sure can!

dialogues.speaker: Tolfin
dialogues.text: What reliable companions you are. Well then, I hope to hear good news from you soon!

dialogues.speaker: Zhorik Shesternin
dialogues.text: Maybe there are others...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Those shiny things we collected earlier... they look like pictures. But where's the Proof of the Cognoscenti? Paimon doesn't see anything like that at all...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: If someone already took it, then that guy was leading us around all this time, wasn't he? Ugh. That's it. That's one score we've gotta settle!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm... Not that we can do anything about that right now, though. Let's go back first!

choices.text: The experiences and memories we gain are the most precious of treasures!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh huh, and adventurers would've all starved to death long ago if that was always the case!

dialogues.speaker: Zhorik Shesternin
dialogues.text: Haha, you're too late. You didn't find the Proof of the Cognoscenti up there, did you?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? How did you...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Sure, but we found something more precious still!

dialogues.speaker: Zhorik Shesternin
dialogues.text: More precious? Impossible...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Judging by that smug look he's wearing, he probably found the Proof ahead of us. Might as well try to trick him here...)

dialogues.speaker: Tolfin
dialogues.text: (Oh? You want me to play along with your little act, then?)

dialogues.speaker: Tolfin
dialogues.text: Well... there are five Proofs of the Cognoscenti after all, nor would locating the Great Treasure be a simple affair even after one collects them all.

dialogues.speaker: Tolfin
dialogues.text: So... I would hardly be surprised if something in Papa Wrench's collection could far surpass a single Proof in value.

dialogues.speaker: Zhorik Shesternin
dialogues.text: ...Such an item exists?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: O—Of course! You could call it priceless, even!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #(Paimon has no idea what {NICKNAME}'s up to, but... That isn't exactly a lie, right? Memories are priceless! Besides...)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...J—Just ask Tolfin or something. He'd pick what we've got over the Proof for sure!

dialogues.speaker: Zhorik Shesternin
dialogues.text: And what would a wandering merchant like him know? ... Aha! I get it now, brat. You're bitter because you lost, aren't you? You're upset that I didn't need to play your little game to get the treasure.

dialogues.speaker: Zhorik Shesternin
dialogues.text: I happen to be in a good mood, so I'll pass this advice to you for free: Forget about the rules. People who stick to them hardly ever get the life they desire.

dialogues.speaker: Zhorik Shesternin
dialogues.text: Fortune favors those who think outside the box, like me. See? You did all that work, in the end, you still couldn't find the Proof of the Cognoscenti.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Zhorik takes out a pristine and opulent goblet. It is hard to believe that it also belonged to Papa Wrench's collection...

dialogues.speaker: Tolfin
dialogues.text: Ah, yes. It is indeed true that one of the five Proofs of the Cognoscenti is a goblet. But as far as I know, that one is in the Fatui's possession. Many treasure hunters have their eyes on it, in fact.

dialogues.speaker: Tolfin
dialogues.text: The Proof that Papa Wrench found was a mask, and he would often let the children play with it.

dialogues.speaker: Tolfin
dialogues.text: As for this goblet... I do believe it's a gift the caravan leader brought from Snezhnograd. Ah, but Papa Wrench never could bring himself to use such a precious thing.

dialogues.speaker: Tolfin
dialogues.text: #It's valuable, of course, but nothing compared to the Proof of the Cognoscenti... Which in turn makes it even less valuable than the treasure {NICKNAME} found, I fear.

dialogues.speaker: Zhorik Shesternin
dialogues.text: That's impossible...

dialogues.speaker: Tolfin
dialogues.text: It appears even a seasoned collector such as you can be mistaken at times, Mr. Shesternin. If it sets your mind at ease, you are free to find an appraiser for it when you return to Novokitezhgrad.

dialogues.speaker: Zhorik Shesternin
dialogues.text: ...Where is the real Proof of the Cognoscenti then? No... forget that. What's the treasure you spoke of, kid? The one you claim is the superior find...

dialogues.speaker: Zhorik Shesternin
dialogues.text: You may have beaten me, but I shan't accept it until you've shown me what you found.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Th—That's...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: (The picture and memories might be priceless to Tolfin, but could we really say something like "This is the most valuable treasure!" without embarrassing ourselves!?)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #(Hurry, {NICKNAME}! Think of something!)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Since there's more to what happened aboard the "Fortunate One" ten years ago...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Before we show you, take a look at this.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You show the picture from earlier to Zhorik...

dialogues.speaker: Zhorik Shesternin
dialogues.text: ...What is this trickery!? Who commissioned you to do this? Was it that old man? Is he still alive? Where is he!?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So you *are* the Zhorik that Papa Wrench mentioned!

dialogues.speaker: Zhorik Shesternin
dialogues.text: "Papa Wrench"... So, he lured me here with a fake name so he can have his revenge, is that it? You think you can take me?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Revenge? What are you talking about?... Wait, so the one who pushed Papa Wrench off the ship was...

dialogues.speaker: Zhorik Shesternin
dialogues.text: Drop the act. You're all working for that old man, aren't you? Wait... Does Danyusha know? Is she in on this too?

dialogues.speaker: Zhorik Shesternin
dialogues.text: That woman... She agreed so quickly because she knew this was a trap all along, didn't she? Offering to deliver the letter, doing all that, just to isolate me...?

response.speaker: Zhorik Shesternin
response.text: No. Not one of you will ever get me! Not you, and not that old man!

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Zhorik scurries away, not even bothering with the precious goblet he mistook for the Proof of the Cognoscenti...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Are you just letting him go? We don't have any grudge against him, but isn't Papa Wrench your friend?

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: Don't worry. The path he took looks most dangerous. I would not be surprised if something happens to him.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What do you mean...?

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: I mean that Papa Wrench has many other friends aside from me. Besides, who doesn't love a story where justice is served?

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: I'm afraid ten years wasn't long enough to change his ways. If he had proven himself a changed man, even just a little, then I would have forgiven him, per Papa Wrench's wishes.

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: Alas, like many others, he too is a prisoner to his baser instincts. What a tragedy.

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: ...What saddens me more is the lack of a winner in our little treasure-hunting game. *sigh* No new story material for me, then.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh! Paimon almost forgot — where exactly is the Proof of the Cognoscenti? Will we find it here? Um... can we ask Huginn for help?

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: Might this be what you're looking for?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: A mask... Is this it!? But how... You had it on you this whole time?

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: Haha, not quite. Zhorik did find it first, but he thought the flashier, fancier goblet was the real Proof, so he tossed the mask aside.

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: And now that he's forfeited it, the treasure is yours.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Feels like a freebie... but wait! We worked hard for it too! It's our just reward!

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: That's right. If you end up revealing the Great Treasure's secrets... Well, that would make for a fascinating story.

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: You land in a safe place...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This deep underground? It doesn't look like there would be a workshop here at all... more like a mole's house than anything else!

dialogues.speaker: Danyusha Shesternin
dialogues.text: Zhorik, I know you'll still think me delusional, even if I tell you all this. But don't you think this is an opportunity?

dialogues.speaker: Zhorik Shesternin
dialogues.text: ...Hmm. Opportunity, you say?

dialogues.speaker: Zhorik Shesternin
dialogues.text: What... What have you done!? This thing's moving, but how do I operate it...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It dropped the lever and ran away? Tch, what does that weasel thief want with this thing anyway...

dialogues.speaker: Tolfin
dialogues.text: Alright, let's head back. If we take too long, Mr. Shesternin might find the treasure before we do.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #That's right! {NICKNAME}, we can't lose to him!
